title: Adapt Register, Audience & Tone
outcome: Ask the same two missing questions to a friend and an organizer, adapting wording appropriately without changing the request or inventing unknown facts.

lessons: Tone is a choice for the reader and purpose, not a ladder from bad to good. Peer messages may be informal and excellent.
A wording change must preserve the communicative action. Replacing 'Where do we meet?' with 'Please confirm the price' changes the question, not just the tone.

demo.prompt: Ask friend Sam and exhibition organizer Mr. Lin the closing time and whether reservations are required at a community photography show; neither answer is given.
steps: Both readers receive the SAME two missing facts: closing time and reservations.
Hi Sam! Do you know what time the photo exhibition closes? Also, do we need to reserve a place? Thanks!
Hello Mr. Lin, could you please tell me the exhibition closing time and whether visitors need to reserve a place? Thank you.
Greeting and courtesy differ while both questions remain.
Overformal legal-style phrasing or dropping one of the questions is not an improvement.
Adjust tone according to the person; never invent the time or booking policy.

teaching.a1: Hi … / Do you know …? / Thanks!; Hello … / Could you please tell me …? / Thank you.
teaching.b1: Compare a long ceremonial request with a short courteous one.

cycleA.prompt: A school science poster competition notice does not state submission deadline or whether posters must be digital or printed. Ask Jo, a classmate, and teacher Ms. Park for BOTH facts. Do not guess answers.

objective.question: Which courteous question retains deadline and format?

options.text: Hey Jo, did you see my new phone?
Dear Ms. Park, please accept my winning poster tomorrow.
options.rationale: Assumes date/submission and asks neither fact.

options.text: Hello Ms. Park, could you please tell me the poster deadline and whether we should submit a digital or printed poster? Thank you.
options.rationale: Right reader and both unknown details.

options.text: Science posters are good. I demand an answer now.

objective.question: Which natural peer message asks the SAME two facts?

options.text: Hi Jo! Do you know when the poster is due and if it needs to be digital or printed? Thanks!
Dear Competition Authority, I formally certify all poster rules.
Hi Jo, the deadline is certainly Friday, and printed posters are banned.
Hi Jo, which science project did you do last year?
Both ask deadline and format; register varies by audience
Teacher asks deadline and peer asks about an unrelated sport
options.rationale: This would change the original intention.

options.text: Both messages announce assumed rules

ownFields.label: Your courteous rewrite of 'Give me the poster details now' asking BOTH missing questions
Why is your changed wording suitable for Ms. Park?

cycleB.prompt: A neighbourhood public mural walk notice omits starting time and meeting point. Write TWO original messages: one to Luca, a friend who signed up, and one to coordinator Ms. Rivera. Both need the same two missing facts. Explain TWO purposeful wording changes. Do not invent the answers or a confirmed booking.

taskStrip.task: Request practical information from a friend and an event coordinator
taskStrip.mustInclude: Starting time AND meeting point in BOTH messages; two changes explained
taskStrip.boundary: Neither fact known; no fake booking, deadlines or demands

fields.label: Your note identifying BOTH missing questions
Original message to coordinator Ms. Rivera
First deliberate wording change and why
Second deliberate wording change and why

cycleB.a1: Use brief general greeting/question starters; do not fill in an unknown answer.
cycleB.b1: Try shortening the organizer request while retaining both questions and courtesy.

transfer.prompt: A youth center beginner dance workshop notice does not say which shoes to bring or whether prior experience is necessary. Ask friend Noa and the registration officer the SAME TWO questions without inventing answers. Explain one audience-related wording change.

fields.label: Why does your wording suit the two readers?

extras.prompt: Ask history teacher Mr. Dao where to submit a class project; location unknown.
extras.question: Which message fits both reader and request?

options.text: Yo, where's my project? Hurry up.
The project is definitely due at the gym.
Hello Mr. Dao, could you please tell me where to submit our history projects? Thank you.
options.rationale: Courteous, correct action, no invented fact.

options.text: Dear District Mayor, I strongly request a new road.

extras.prompt: Ask close friend Eli when a school music rehearsal starts.
extras.question: Which is clearest natural peer wording?

options.text: Hi Eli, do you know what time rehearsal starts? Thanks!
To Whom It May Concern: Pursuant to the rehearsal regulations …
You must tell me now or I will report you.
Music rehearsals are musical.

extras.prompt: Politely ask a bus-tour guide BOTH starting place and finishing time.
extras.question: Which preserves both questions?

options.text: Dear Guide, your tour sounds amazing.
Could you please confirm where the tour begins?
Please change the tour to Sunday afternoon.
Could you please tell me where the tour begins and what time it ends? Thank you.

extras.prompt: Ask a museum volunteer coordinator if students may volunteer at a weekend session. Permission not yet granted.
extras.question: Which request is accurate?

options.text: We will attend as approved volunteers; your permission is confirmed.
Hello, could you please let us know whether students may volunteer at the weekend session?
I command you to approve all students immediately.
I have already accepted the post on your behalf.

aiLens: Review the two saved messages plus sharedIntent and changes. Both must ask starting time and meeting point; do not auto-detect missing meaning by literal keywords. Allow natural friend voice and varied polite coordinator phrasing. Never ghostwrite both messages.
